kenton-county-public-library-covington-b: Turn right on Scott Blvd. Our free parking is available in the lot on the left directly past the library. Parking: The Covington Library has a free parking lot for our visitors. Please note that free parking may not be available at all times, especially during popular events Metered parking and a fee-based parking garage are also available. Street meters are free after 4 pm and on weekends.
TANK bus serves the Covington Library.

Homebound services are designed to offer library materials and programming to Kenton County residents with a short or long-term disability, or a medical condition that prevents them from visiting the Library .
Free deliveries of any available materials are made monthly. This includes books, CDs, audiobooks, DVDs, etc.
All meeting rooms are accessible and have power outlets.
Library drive-thru closes one hour before the branch.
campbell-county-public-library-newport-b: If you are a resident of Campbell County and cannot visit the library because of temporary or permanent illness or disability, you are eligible for our home delivery service. Materials available for delivery include regular print books, large print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs. Materials are selected based on your reading interests and needs. The Adult Outreach Services Assistant will deliver the materials to your home on a specified day. You may also sign up to have your materials delivered by mail for free.

Through a national network of cooperating libraries, the NLS administers a free library program of braille and audio materials circulated to eligible borrowers in the United States by postage-free mail. Kentucky Talking Books Talking Book Service is available through the Kentucky Talking Book Library. This service is provided free of charge to anyone unable to read because of a visual or physical limitation.
If you are interested in signing up for any of the free services below or would like more information, please call our Adult Outreach Services Assistant at 859-572-5035, ext. 352.

You can call or email us if you need help accessing your account or placing a hold. Search for an item in our catalog and click "Request Item" to place it on hold. Wait for a phone call, text, email or postal mail notifying you that your holds are ready for pickup. Follow instructions for curbside pickup below. Picking Up Items You will be notified by phone, text, email or postal mail when your holds are available for curbside pickup. Please note that your holds are not ready for pickup until you receive a notification and the items are marked as "Held" in your account.

Park in one of the parking spots that are designated for curbside pickup. Let us know that you are outside by calling the number listed on the parking spot's sign. We will need your name, library card number and parking spot number. If a staff member doesn't answer, do not leave a voicemail message. Please call back until a staff member answers. Remain in your vehicle. A staff member will place your items directly in your vehicle, preferably into your trunk.
Curbside pickup is available for current physical library card holders. The service is not available for digital library card holders.

You will have seven days to pick up your holds. Q: What if the parking spots designated for curbside pickup are full? A: If the parking spots are full, please park in another area of the parking lot until one is available. We will only deliver items to vehicles parked in the designated spots. Q: Who can pick up my items? A: Anyone may pick up your items. They must have your library card number in order to do so. Staff will not release items to those without a library card number.
Q: How long will I have to pick up my holds once I have been notified that they are ready? A: You will have seven days to pick up your holds.
